verdicts.reason: The helper test file imports only _are_all_projects_error_upsampled/_is_error_focused_query/_should_apply_sample_weight_transform/transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling, never the newly-caching is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects; BaseTestCase._pre_setup calls cache.clear() per test so a 60s stale entry can never survive; and both error fixtures in OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest carry contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate=0.1, so no fixture exercises a missing sample_weight.

count() declares default_result_type="integer" while upsampled_count declares "number" even though its aggregate is wrapped in toInt64; get_json_meta_type resolves meta from the SnQLFunction's declared result type, so swapping count() for upsampled_count() changes the reported field type in the response meta.

The option's registered default is indeed [] with FLAG_AUTOMATOR_MODIFIABLE, but whether a rollout is underway and whether any profile identified options.get as a hotspot lives in production option state and the PR description, neither of which is in this checkout; a link to the profile/dashboard or the current prod option value would settle it.

upsampled_count carries no private=True (unlike neighbouring column_hash/examples/rounded_timestamp), and is_accessible only gates functions marked private, so any caller can pass yAxis=upsampled_count() and bypass the allowlist; DiscoverDatasetConfig is also loaded for Dataset.Transactions/Events/IssuePlatform where Column("sample_weight") is not a supported column.

The diff replaces sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1)) with sum(sample_weight); _derive_client_error_sampling_rate only writes data["sample_rate"] when an error_sampling context exists and 0 < rate <= 1, so events in allowlisted projects lacking it get no weight and drop out of the sum, and the codebase's own _get_error_weighted_times_seen explicitly falls back to 1 in exactly that case.

The only place a falsy sample rate is skipped is _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling in the test factory, a file this PR does not touch, and the fragment states no problem — a 0.0 client sample rate is meaningless anyway, and the production path (_derive_client_error_sampling_rate) already rejects it explicitly.

Grepping the whole working tree for invalidate_upsampling_cache returns only its own definition — no caller, signal receiver, or options-change hook — so the cache added in the same commit has no invalidation path other than its 60s TTL.

The commit adds a mode-160000 gitlink named sentry-repo at the repository root pointing at commit a5d290951def, with nothing to do with error upsampling; it is plainly a nested clone left behind by the development environment.

allowlist comes back from options.get as a Sequence (list), and the membership test `all(project_id in allowlist for project_id in project_ids)` is O(len(allowlist)) per project; converting to a set first would make it O(1) — and this is the very lookup the PR claims to be optimising.

The transform only matches the exact string "count()" after lower/strip, but yAxis values come straight from request.GET.getlist("yAxis") and FUNCTION_PATTERN explicitly accepts an `as <alias>` suffix, so `count() as errors` parses fine downstream yet silently skips upsampling.

_is_error_focused_query does a bare `"event.type:error" in query`, so `!event.type:error` (which excludes errors) matches and returns True, while `event.type: error` does not match and returns False; both edge cases are as described.

With transformAliasToInputFormat=1 process_results renames the result key from the alias `count` to function_alias_map's raw field text `upsampled_count() as count`, while resolve_axis_column returns the untransformed query_columns[0] (`count()`); the serializer then does r.get(column, 0) and emits 0 for every bucket.

verdicts.evidence: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:27,73; grep of src/ for cache-key construction
verdicts.reason: These are the only two places in src/ that build a cache key from Python's hash(); the other hash(tuple(...)) uses are __hash__ implementations. Everywhere else keys are readable concatenations (e.g. src/sentry/tasks/post_process.py:79) or an explicit md5_text digest, so an opaque signed int here cannot be traced back to a project set when debugging.

The key is org id plus a hash of the project id set only — the allowlist value that produced the cached boolean is not part of it — and invalidate_upsampling_cache(organization_id, project_ids) can only delete a key if the caller already knows the exact project-id combination that was queried; nothing in the repo records those combinations, so in practice only the 60s TTL clears anything.

The upsampled_count snql_aggregate lambda takes `args` and never uses it (required_args is empty); the count() definition a few hundred lines above in the same dict uses `lambda _, alias:` for exactly this case. The diff rewrote this lambda's body, so it is squarely in scope.

The errors-storage column definition lives in the Snuba repo, not this checkout, so I cannot say whether sample_weight is Nullable(UInt64) or has a non-null default. Either way the undercount in c005 holds; the Snuba storage YAML for the errors entity would settle which shape it takes.

PYTHONHASHSEED randomisation applies to str/bytes/datetime, not ints; SnubaParams.project_ids returns a sorted list[int], and hash((1,2,3)) is identical across processes (verified by running it under PYTHONHASHSEED=random three times, whereas hash(('a','b')) varied). The keys do match across workers, so the stated mechanism is wrong.

All three are as described: the NOTE at :49-53 claims the allowlist is read fresh every call and that this is intentional, immediately below a caller that caches it for 60s; the "safe because allowlist changes are infrequent" line at :23-25 asserts a property nothing establishes; and "we rely on the database schema to ensure sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects" is contradicted by _derive_client_error_sampling_rate, which leaves sample_rate unset whenever the context is absent or out of range.

The repo default really is CACHES = {"default": DummyCache}, and sentry.utils.cache.cache is just django.core.cache.cache; what production actually configures lives in getsentry deployment config that is not in this checkout, so the effect of the new cache cannot be determined here.

_get_event_stats passes the closed-over `dataset`, not its own `scoped_dataset` parameter, to is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects; get_event_stats_factory calls _get_event_stats with split_dataset = discover on the dashboard-widget-split path while the outer dataset is metrics_enhanced_performance, and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns False for metrics datasets, so upsampling is skipped there even with every project allowlisted. (Pre-existing, but in the function this PR rewrites.)
Same gitlink as c008; I confirmed there is no .gitmodules file anywhere in the checkout, so the 160000 entry is an unregistered submodule that will leave an empty directory on clone.

_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling exists only in the test factory, which this PR does not touch, and its `if client_sample_rate:` guard already excludes 0, so the cited example is wrong; the real ingest path validates 0 < rate <= 1 and logs/metrics anything outside it.

OptionsStore.get calls get_cache, which checks the in-process _local_cache dict before touching the network cache, so the 'expensive repeated option lookups' being cached away are normally a dict hit; the replacement sentry.utils.cache.cache is django.core.cache, i.e. a memcached/redis round trip in any non-dummy production config, so the stated rationale is backwards.
_are_all_projects_error_upsampled takes `organization: Organization` and its body never references it — the allowlist is a global option keyed only by project id.

The single pre-diff `if should_upsample: final_columns = transform(...)` is now repeated in the top_events, use_rpc and default branches; I traced all four return paths (top_events x use_rpc) and each still receives the transform, so behaviour is unchanged and the only effect is three copies to keep in sync. The sub-assertion about a never-read alias is imprecise — `upsampling_enabled` is read three times — but it is a pointless rename of `should_upsample` one line earlier.
The identical call transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns) now appears at three separate points inside _get_event_stats where one call before the branching would do.
